title: Bookmarking Feature Handoff Plan
purpose: Proposed handoff assembled from source-linked outcomes; human source review and approval required.

scope.text: Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.
Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.

requirements.text: Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.
Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.

stories.text: Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.
acceptance_criteria: After a reader bookmarks an article, the article is recorded as bookmarked for that reader and can be observed as bookmarked when the reader returns to it.
The bookmark action has an effect beyond the initiating control: the article appears among that reader's bookmarked articles on a later access.

stories.text: Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark.
acceptance_criteria: After a reader removes a bookmark, the article is no longer recorded as bookmarked for that reader and is observed as unbookmarked when the reader returns to it.
The removal has an effect beyond the initiating control: the article does not appear among that reader's bookmarked articles on a later access.
A bookmark created for a reader remains available as bookmarked after the reader signs out and signs back in.
The bookmark state is not lost or reset by ending one sign-in session and starting another.

open_questions: The source does not specify whether a reader must be signed in at the time of creating or removing a bookmark, or how an anonymous action is associated with a later sign-in.
When does the persistence window for a bookmark start: at the moment the bookmark is created, at the next sign-out, or at another event?
Is persistence measured in sign-in sessions, elapsed time, calendar time, or a combination, and how are concurrent sessions treated?
At what exact point does a bookmark stop being available, and is the final sign-in session included in the persistence window?
What observable state should result after the persistence window ends, if it ends at all—should the bookmark become unavailable, be hidden, or require recovery?
How does a reader supply a bookmark or unbookmark request, and how are the reader's sign-in identity and article identity transmitted so the backend can persist the action?
What success, failure, already-bookmarked, already-unbookmarked, and error/empty/exhaustion responses can the interface return, and how should each be interpreted by the reader?
Which user-visible behaviors apply under each response contract—for example, when to show a bookmark confirmation, retry option, or sign-in prompt—without assuming a particular API protocol?
Who is responsible for delivering the bookmarking feature, and what authority do they have over the acceptance criteria?
What is the delivery date or milestone for the bookmarking feature?
